title: Detection of extragalactic CF<SUP>+</SUP> toward PKS 1830-211. Chemical differentiation in the absorbing gas
question: Is CF+ present in the z=0.89 molecular absorber toward PKS 1830-211, what is its abundance, and how does its line profile compare with other species?

data.sensitivity: NE rms ~0.001 of continuum per 2.6 km/s channel; opacity uncertainty 0.003 (1 sigma)

what.value: Line frequencies and molecular data from CDMS

evidence.quote: Frequencies and molecular data are taken from the Cologne Database for Molecular Spectroscopy ((cite: mul01)).

what.value: H2 column density 2e22 cm-2 toward SW

evidence.quote: With a H$_2$ column density of 2$\times$10$^{22}$ cm$^{-2}$ ((cite: mul14a))
we compare the new spectra obtained in 2014 with those of the same lines observed in 2012 ((cite: mul14a), ALMA Cycle 0 data)
Hence their rotation temperature is equal to 5.14 K, the CMB temperature at z=0.89 ((cite: mul13)).

recipe.goal: Extract spectra of both lensed images
recipe.method: Fit two-point-source model to visibilities with UVMULTIFIT
Integrate opacity over -20 to +20 km/s, convert with alpha assuming excitation coupled to CMB
assumptions: Tex = 5.14 K (CMB at z=0.89); hyperfine splitting neglected; optically thin

recipe.method: Divide by N(H2)=2e22 cm-2; compare with cosmic fluorine abundance; steady-state CF+/HF ratio from rate coefficients
assumptions: Fluorine abundance in absorber similar to cosmic; T=100 K; [e]≈[C+]

evidence.quote: The associated uncertainty is of 0.003 at 1$\sigma$.
we conclude that only $\sim$1% of the interstellar fluorine is captured in CF$^+$
much narrower than the absorption line width ($\sim$15 km s$^{-1}$, FWHM)
